segments: again the Arabs, and they said to him
that, like the kings before him, he should conduct himself with moderation.
He, however, answered them,
"Since I am king,
whatever I wish, I do."
Then they separated from him, becoming enraged.
And they gathered against him again, armed and shouting,
"Either change your conduct,
or you shall die immediately!"
He, however, wrote to Mu'awiyah to send him an army.
The Arabs, however, acted quickly,
and with violence rushed upon him and killed him.
Mu'awiyah had sent an army with Habib,
and when they arrived at Bostra
and heard that Uthman was killed,
they left off and turned back.
[The] 4th [caliph]:
[After] {OCR?} Uthman, Ali ibn Abi Talib [reigned] five years in Yathrib and in Babylon (Iraq) alone,
because Syria and Egypt were with Mu'awiyah.
And in the year 968
[968] of the Greeks (657 of our Lord?), the two sides clashed with one another.
And when many from both sides were destroyed,
Mu'awiyah turned back without bowing to Ali.
And they clashed with one another again,
and many were killed between them.
Then three zealots set out to go and kill these three on whose account war had fallen among the Arabs:
Ali, Mu'awiyah, and Habib (and Sa'id), the general in Egypt.
Therefore, the one who went to Egypt was seized and killed,
and likewise the one who went to the camp of Mu'awiyah.
The third, however, entered the camp of Ali,
and pierced him with a lance and killed him.
Then the Arabs in the east and in the west submitted to Mu'awiyah.
And he transferred the kingdom from Yathrib to the city of Damascus.
[Mu'awiyah ruled {OCR?}] after Ali nineteen years.
For indeed even in the days of Uthman, for fifteen years, Mu'awiyah himself governed Palestine,
and likewise also in these five years of Ali—
all together thirty-nine years.
In the year 977
(977 of the Greeks,

and sent to Mu'awiyah a man named Sergius, saying:
"Give me assistance,
and I will subject all of Romania (the Byzantine Empire) to you."
